scope: FP-DIVPRE-SLOTRES-CUT2: break T-20260902-043 signoff setup top scalar_unit g_iter.div_pre.sig[245] -> fp_exec slot_result_r[9] (54 levels, 25.589 ns, -5.047 ns) by predecoding the 256-bit leading-one index into div_pre/sqrt_pre capture and using the registered index in round_pack; no new pipeline latency, no DSP, no SDC false_path.

implementation.summary: In release FP_ITER=1 g_iter, added lead[7:0]/lead_valid to fp_pre_t and predecode the highest set bit of the iterative FDIV/FSQRT quotient in div_finish_pre/sqrt_finish_pre at the same cycle div_pre/sqrt_pre is captured. The original round_pack was split into round_pack_h (takes a precomputed leading-one index) and a public round_pack wrapper that preserves the old scan for all non-iterative callers. finish_pre uses round_pack_h when lead_valid is set, removing the 256-bit priority scan from div_pre.sig -> slot_result_r while keeping exact rounding semantics.

semantics.raw_bit: unchanged; round_pack_h is line-for-line the original round_pack body with the leading-one supplied from the registered index; all existing round_pack callers use the unchanged public wrapper
semantics.commit_order: unchanged; no new pipeline state or latency; single outstanding fp_exec transaction and one held response preserved
semantics.fpsr_fpcr: unchanged; FPCR snapshot at acceptance and FPSR sticky OR preserved
semantics.fcmp_nzcv: unchanged; CMP remains on existing pp_other path
semantics.kill_reset: unchanged; lead/lead_valid are part of existing fp_pre_t registers and are cleared with those registers on reset/kill

implementation.notes: No DSP added. Storage increase is 9 bits per fp_pre_t instance (lead[7:0] + lead_valid). No latency change, so no testbench latency updates were required. The priority scan is moved earlier in the iterative path instead of being duplicated.
